categories.name: It works
categories.notes: dotnet build succeeds with 0 errors and 0 warnings: 5/5. GET / returns 200 and is the blog front page, through the 'Blog' node with domain '/'. It has a hero, a welcome rich text and a blogPostListBlock showing both posts as cards with image, date, title and teaser, and both links work: 10/10. Both posts render every block (richTextBlock, imageBlock including a half-width image next to half-width text, quoteBlock), with no 'Could not render' or exception text: 10/10. All 5 media items are the provided Unsplash photos, imported via MCP create-media into a 'Blog' media folder and served through GetCropUrl URLs, and 7/7 images load. The model also fixed the left-edge focal points that MCP create-media sets: 5/5. The domain '/' is assigned on the Blog page, and all content is published: 5/5.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: heroBlock, richTextBlock, imageBlock, quoteBlock and blogPostListBlock are elements in Blocks. seoComposition is an element in Compositions. blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages, and siteRoot stays in Repositories: 8/8. Both pages use a block grid, each with its own data type ('Blog Front Page Grid', 'Blog Post Grid'). The block set is reusable and its properties make sense (heading/subheading/backgroundImage, text, image/caption, quote/attribution, heading/maxItems), and the posts are spread over 5 to 7 blocks with full and half column spans: 7/7. siteRoot is the only type allowed at root and allows blogFrontPage, which allows only blogPost. Templates are assigned, aliases are camelCase, and the grids sit in /Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid: 5/5. The composition holds only SEO meta (metaTitle, metaDescription). Post metadata (teaser, publishDate, mainImage) are real properties, and nothing is duplicated or orphaned: 5/5.

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: blogFrontPage.cshtml and blogPost.cshtml call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "blocks"), and the scaffold's blockgrid partials are untouched: 7/7. There are 5 adapters in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml. Each takes BlockGridItem<T>, maps to a plain model and calls Component.InvokeAsync, with no markup. The list adapter gets its posts from the injected BlogPostService: 6/6. There are 5 ViewComponents with Default.cshtml views under Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/, typed to plain models in Models/Blocks and Models/Blog, with no Umbraco dependencies: 7/7. Program.cs and appsettings.json are untouched, and there are no migrations. BlogPostService is registered by Composers/BlogComposer.cs. The code uses friendly extensions (AncestorOrSelf, Children<T>, Url(), GetCropUrl), with no injected URL services. Styling goes through the Tailwind/Vite pipeline into wwwroot/dist/site.css, with block-grid layout CSS and rich-text styles added: 5/5.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Post 1, 'MCP is the USB-C port for AI', is substantive and accurate. It covers the MxN integration problem, client/server, tools/resources/prompts, JSON-RPC over stdio/HTTP, and permission control. Post 2, 'Your CMS, now with a conversation', shows MCP in practice, with a side-by-side image and text, a pull quote and a 'where this goes next' section. Both are several paragraphs over several blocks, with relevant cable and puzzle photos and photographer credits: 6/6. The presentation is polished: a dark image hero, a 2-column card grid, a post header with back link, date, title and teaser, a wide header image, and a readable prose column with a styled blockquote and figure captions: 4/4.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Channel and order 2/3. All schema, media, content and the domain went through Umbraco MCP (60 calls, 39 writes), with no browser, Management API, DB, uSync writes or migrations. The order held: model, then content, then stop Umbraco (06:27:38), then write Razor, then build and restart (06:29:49), with no warnings. There was no memory access and no references to the bench folder. Small stray: its verification step wrote curl output to /tmp and headless-Edge screenshots to %TEMP% (front.png, post.png), then read them back. That is outside the project folder (process.stayedInFolder FAIL). Final report 2/2: it is accurate and complete. It discloses the focal-point fix, the MCP template placeholder behaviour, and the leftover .umbraco-run.log, and it claims nothing false.

summary: A complete, polished MCP-built blog. It has 5 reusable blocks, a proper page/block/composition model, a textbook adapter-to-ViewComponent pipeline, a Tailwind design and two substantive, accurate posts about MCP. The only blemish is a small stray outside the project folder (temp files from its own verification).
strengths: Clean schema: 5 blocks in Blocks, an SEO-only composition, separate front page and post grids in /Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid, and real teaser/publishDate/mainImage properties
Textbook rendering pipeline: GetBlockGridHtmlAsync -> markup-free adapters -> ViewComponents with plain models; the post query lives in BlogPostService
Polished, real-blog presentation with a hero, card grid, readable post column and half-width image/text layouts
Noticed and fixed the left-edge focal points set by MCP create-media, and disclosed it in the report
Correct order of operations, with Razor written only after stopping Umbraco
